doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: New York studio and TV work
title: Racial mix of studio musicians; his four children
summary: Studio rhythm sections were mixed and often uncredited; he mentions his four musical children.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: There was something I wanted to ask you about the studio scene that you were so much a part of. What was the racial make-up of the studio musicians at that time?

Oh there were a lot of blacks and all mixed in. In fact all the rhythm sections were that, and they had horn players, and before we got out of the business we had a violin section. But nobody knew who was playing because half the time they wouldn’t put your name on the record. But if you wanted a good feel, you had a great mixture of different people.
Yeah every one of them play something.
